declarations.checkedType: agent(max_characters?: integer, url: string) -> string with throw[api_error | auth_error | fetch_error] | io
declarations.documentation:
Tool: fetch a web page over HTTP GET and return its body text, cut to @max_characters@ code points
(the budget covers the whole answer, and a cut page says how long the page really was). A non-2xx
status throws `http.api_failure` — `http.auth_error` for 401 / 403, `http.api_error` otherwise, each
carrying the status and the server's own body; a request that never completes throws
`http.fetch_error`.
declarations.name: fetch_page

parameters.documentation: The budget for the whole answer, in code points.
parameters.label: max_characters

max_characters.description: The budget for the whole answer, in code points.

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for something other than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is
not 401 / 403. Which failures are worth repeating is read off @status@ — 408 / 429 / 5xx are the
transient ones, and every other status repeats its answer until the argument changes — which is why
the status rides on the error rather than being folded into a sentence. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body verbatim.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over the identity of the caller: the endpoint answered 401 or
403, so the credential is what failed — revoked, expired, or scoped too narrowly. Retrying with the
same credential gives the same answer; the recovery is a fresh resolution of it, so the ordinary
composition is a `supervise` converter signalling `supervise.interrupted`. @context@ says which call
failed in the caller's own words and @message@ carries the server's own body, kept apart so a renderer
can show either alone.

403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion; a quota 403 that is
replayed answers the same way.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

declarations.signature: agent fetch_page(url: string, max_characters: integer ?= 16000) -> string
